campaign_name: Save Dallas City Hall charter amendment petition
purpose: Charter amendment naming 1500 Marilla (I.M. Pei City Hall) as the seat of government and requiring a public election before city operations can move out of City Hall
sponsor: Save Dallas City Hall Coalition. Donors reported include attorney Ben Abbott and descendants of Margaret McDermott and former Mayor Erik Jonsson. Backers include Councilman Adam Bazaldua, Leiane Pei and architect Tipton Housewright
circulation_firm: unknown (no firm named in sources; LMK Strategies connection not verified)
signatures_required: 20,000 valid signatures from registered Dallas voters
deadline: Sources conflict: D Magazine (Sep 24, 2026) says collection runs to mid-January 2027. Fox 4 says the notice of intent was to be filed Oct 2, 2026 with 60 days to collect (about early Dec 2026). Target is the May 2027 ballot
budget_or_spend: unknown (privately funded by the donors named above)
decision_maker: Save Dallas City Hall Coalition leadership (individual names unknown beyond backers listed)
evidence_note: The drive launched with events in Far North Dallas and East Dallas, and gathering at midterm polling places was described as likely. The Oct 20, 2026 D Magazine piece '4 Dallas petition drives voters should know about' is behind Cloudflare and could not be read, so the other three drives in it are unknown. Highest-value Texas lead: it is well funded, the deadline is near and polling-place collection on Nov 3 is likely.

campaign_name: Other Dallas petition drives in D Magazine Oct 20, 2026 article (3 of 4 unidentified)
signatures_required: unknown (Dallas charter amendment petitions need 20,000 valid signatures)
evidence_note: Article exists (title confirmed via search) but fetch blocked by Cloudflare. Recall drives against Council members Chad West and Gay Donnell Willis failed in July 2026 (KERA via D Magazine Leading Off Jul 24, 2026); next council election Nov 2027. Recommend manual read of the article.

pay_rate: $34-50/hr (as reported in task brief; not independently verified)
evidence_note: Three web searches found no LMK Strategies posting or firm page, so the petition it is hiring for could not be identified. The posting probably sits on a job board that search does not index. Possible match: Save Dallas City Hall (unverified).

campaign_name: Austin United PAC convention center charter amendment petition
purpose: Charter amendment to halt the $1.6B Austin convention center expansion
evidence_note: The clerk invalidated the petition, the PAC lost at trial and appealed to the Texas Supreme Court. Austin's clerk page lists no active 2026 petitions. No verified petition is circulating in Austin for May 2027. Austin initiative rule: 5% of qualified voters or 20,000, whichever is smaller, and signatures expire after 180 days.

contact: Houston City Secretary: citysecretary@houstontx.gov, 900 Bagby, Houston TX 77002
evidence_note: Searches surfaced only older drives: San Antonio Justice Charter (2023), fire union petitions (2018), and Houston Prop A (2021). None is active for May 2027. Fort Worth charter changes are council-initiated, not petitions. Houston petition signatures must be dated no more than 30 days before filing.

purpose: Recall council members over data center votes
deadline: San Angelo D3 (Harry Thomas) recall election Nov 3, 2026; Granbury petitions in litigation; El Paso unknown
evidence_note: Newsweek roundup: the San Angelo recall is on the Nov 3 ballot, Granbury is still being fought over (the city rejected petitions July 28 and then told an appeals court they would go to council), and El Paso D4 status was not stated. Temple failed. This points to a national trend of data-center recalls, a possible service niche.

campaign_name: Restore Our Fairgrounds racing-ban charter amendment / referendum
purpose: Permanently ban auto racing at the Nashville Fairgrounds Speedway site, which blocks the NASCAR-backed speedway renovation. The job posting ties the campaign to affordable housing
type: Metro charter amendment by citizen petition (referendum)
sponsor: Restore Our Fairgrounds coalition (co-founders Mike Kopp, Saul Solomon; representative John Spragens; drive managed with Stephen Lofton)
deadline: Signatures submitted around Sep 18, 2026. Hearing on withdrawn signatures set for Oct 27, 2026. Election expected in 2027 (NewsChannel 5 says 'next summer'; exact date unknown)
pay_rate: $22/hr circulator, $24/hr team lead, up to $35/hr with bonuses, +$2/hr bilingual
budget_or_spend: unknown (group hired a slate of consultants per Axios)
evidence_note: The Outreach Team's posting dated Jul 17, 2026 names the Restore Our Fairgrounds referendum, so paid circulation is confirmed. Signature collection is over and the measure is certified, so the field phase has ended. The next phase is the 2027 election campaign plus litigation from opponents (Decline to Sign, NOTE, CARE; Holland & Knight letter). Possible future work: GOTV and canvassing.

Two searches found no PS Logistics petition posting or Colorado SOS petition-entity license under that name. Colorado requires petition entities to hold an SOS license (new registration rules took effect Dec 1, 2025), so the SOS petition entity license list is the place to check this manually.

decision_maker: Denver Clerk and Recorder, Elections Division (approves petition formats)
evidence_note: The Denver Ballot Access page blocks automated fetching (robots), and news searches found no approved 2027 Denver initiative. Check the clerk's page by hand.

evidence_note: No Field Manager posting was found. The only Mobilize Michigan posting found is a Field Canvasser job for a voter-contact canvass, not a petition. No petition campaign is tied to Mobilize Michigan.

sponsor: Americans for Citizen Voting-Michigan (chair Paul Jacob; organizer Kurt O'Keefe)

deadline: Planned 'second launch in April 2027' for 2028 ballot

purpose: Recall mayor over handling of proposed data center
sponsor: Michigan Citizens Against Data Centers (spokesperson Paula Caltrider)
evidence_note: The companion recall of Councilwoman Elaine Ferris is on the Nov 3, 2026 ballot (Newsweek). Other Michigan township data-center recalls (Augusta, Frenchtown, Lowell, Van Buren, Lenox) were ongoing or had unclear status as of summer 2026. Lyon Township failed.

campaign_name: Winneconne Community School District board recall
purpose: Recall Board President Kati Calewarts and VP Dean Ackmann
deadline: Appeal to Wisconsin Elections Commission pending (filed about mid-Oct 2026)
signatures_collected: 4,600+ (rejected by clerk Kari Flagg for missing registration/intent filings)
evidence_note: Signatures were thrown out over a procedural filing error, which is exactly the compliance gap a professional firm sells against. The Port Washington mayor recall (data center) failed to submit its 1,591 signatures.

campaign_name: Ottawa data center ban initiative ordinance
purpose: Ban data centers using more than 25 MW within Ottawa city limits
sponsor: Citizen petition led by Jessica Christopher ('We the People Ottawa' per KSHB headline)
deadline: Verified Aug 7, 2026. Commission had 20 days to adopt, otherwise it goes to the voters. Lightfield entitlement period ends Oct 30, 2026
evidence_note: Signature phase complete. A similar Emporia, KS petition (about 1,400 signatures against the Digital Campus, July 2026) was also found, but its article could not be fetched.

No currently active Minneapolis charter petition was found. Spencer, Iowa residents forced a special council election by petition in Feb 2026 (completed). Indiana turned up only Change.org data-center petitions, which are informal and have no legal effect. Nothing verified as active now.

campaign_name: Missouri Right to Education constitutional amendment, 2028 return
purpose: Add a fundamental right to public education to the Missouri Constitution
sponsor: Missouri Right to Education campaign (director Spencer Toder; Missouri NEA coalition member)
signatures_required: 8% of votes in 6 of 8 congressional districts (constitutional amendment rule); exact number unknown
deadline: 2028 cycle (petitions due early May 2028; exact date unknown)
evidence_note: Stopped in Mar 2026 and plans a 2028 return backed by Missouri NEA. The 2026 attempt was underpowered, which makes it a strong prospect for a paid feasibility study. No 2028 petition numbers approved for circulation were verified: the SOS 2028 page could not be fetched and AG opinion searches returned only 2026-cycle petitions.

campaign_name: Respect MO Voters (Amendment 6) and People Not Politicians redistricting referendum (Prop A)
purpose: Respect MO Voters: limit legislative changes to voter-approved initiatives. Prop A: overturn the 2025 congressional map
sponsor: Respect MO Voters (co-founder Benjamin Singer); People Not Politicians PAC
signatures_required: Amendment: 8% in 6 of 8 CDs. Referendum: 5% in 6 of 8 CDs
deadline: Signature phase done; litigation over Nov 3, 2026 ballot placement (Missouri Supreme Court reportedly ordered an initiative back on ballot per Missouri Times; which one not confirmed here)
signatures_collected: Prop A: about 305,000 submitted (about 103,000 ruled invalid as gathered before Oct 14). Respect MO Voters: had enough per SOS preliminary reports
evidence_note: Context only. If Respect MO Voters is defeated or blocked, a 2028 refile is plausible but unverified. No Missouri 2028 petition with paid circulators was found.

purpose: Recall council member over Nebius AI data center tax incentives
evidence_note: Perkins was recalled 68% to 32%. Residents have also called for a data-center moratorium vote. This is a proof case for data-center-opposition petition demand.
